paper_summary: This paper investigates the structure and early evolution of solar coronal mass ejections (CMEs) in the low corona (below 1.3 R⊙) using extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) and white-light observations. The study focuses on the three-part CME structure (leading edge, low-density zone, and core) and correlates EUV appearances with white-light coronagraph images for four limb events. Data are drawn from multiple instruments aboard SDO, STEREO, GOES-16, and SOHO, covering both the low and high corona.

instruments.name: Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) on board the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO)
instruments.general_comments: AIA images the low corona with a field of view (FOV) of 1.3 R⊙, a high cadence of 12 s, and a resolution of 0.6″ per pixel. It provides observations in seven EUV passbands. In this study, AIA data at 193 Å and 131 Å are used to reveal the early three-part appearance of CMEs (leading edge, filament or hot channel, and low-density zone).
supporting_quotes: The AIA records the low corona with the FOV (ﬁeld of view) of 1.3 R⊙, cadence of 12 s and resolution of 0.′′6 per pixel in seven EUV passbands.

instruments.name: Extreme Ultraviolet Imager (EUVI) on board the Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory (STEREO)
instruments.general_comments: EUVI provides solar EUV images at four wavelengths with a field of view of 1.7 R⊙. It partially overlaps with the white-light coronagraph COR1 (FOV of 1.4–4 R⊙) such that continuous observations from the solar surface to the outer corona are possible. Both STEREO-A and STEREO-B are used to capture events from distinct viewing angles.
supporting_quotes: The EUVI provides the solar EUV images at four wavelength with an FOV of 1.7 R⊙, partially overlapping with that of COR1 (1.4–4 R⊙)...

instruments.name: Solar Ultraviolet Imager (SUVI) on board GOES-16
instruments.general_comments: SUVI images the solar corona in six EUV passbands with a horizontal field of view larger than 1.6 R⊙. It is used here to capture the extended corona when AIA’s FOV is limited.
supporting_quotes: The SUVI images the solar corona with an FOV larger than 1.6 R⊙ in the horizontal direction in six EUV passbands.

data_collection_periods.physical_observable: The extended leading edge of the CME, aiding in the reconstruction of the three-part structure by complementing observations from AIA.

instruments.name: COR1 Coronagraph on board STEREO
instruments.general_comments: COR1 is a white-light coronagraph with a field of view of approximately 1.4–4 R⊙. It detects Thomson-scattered light from free electrons, thereby revealing density structures in the corona. It is used in conjunction with EUVI to link observations from the inner corona to the white-light features.
supporting_quotes: The white-light coronagraphs COR1 (Howard et al. 2008) on board the STEREO... are used to analyze the CME structure in the high corona.

data_collection_periods.time_range: Observations at 20:16 UT and twenty minutes later (circa 20:36 UT) on 2013 September 24
data_collection_periods.wavelengths: White-light (imaging Thomson-scattered light from free electrons)
data_collection_periods.physical_observable: Changes in the density structure as the low-corona features (filament/leading edge) evolve into the bright front and core in white-light.

instruments.name: Large Angle and Spectrometric Coronagraph (LASCO) on board the Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SOHO)
instruments.general_comments: LASCO is a white-light coronagraph with a field of view covering 2.2–30 R⊙ (with C2 covering 2.2–6 R⊙ and C3 covering 4–30 R⊙). It detects Thomson-scattered light and is used to monitor CME evolution in the high corona.
supporting_quotes: The Large Angle and Spectrometric Coronagraph (LASCO; Brueckner et al. 1995) on board the Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SOHO)...
